envelope.response:
**Findings after four submissions**

Three ideas failed. Acceleration in average hours, persistence of rises in the stock rate, and a three-month shift between two flow rates each gave near-zero mean rank correlations. Their t-statistics were below one, so all three failed our falsification rule.

One idea worked modestly. Annual hourly-pay growth, standardized against each group's own three-year history, produced a positive rank correlation with a t-statistic just above two. It was stronger in low-T periods. Caveats: coverage dropped to about sixty percent because of the long history requirement, and the signal is highly persistent. Pay-based signals deserve further robustness testing.
